subject: history

items.q: Were the Troubles purely a religious war?
items.correct: No — they were about national identity and politics as much as religion.
items.random_wrong: They were a war between Ireland and France.
items.why: The conflict centred on whether Northern Ireland should stay in the UK or join Ireland.

items.q: Was the 'Irish question' only a 20th-century issue?
items.correct: No — tensions over Ireland's relationship with Britain go back centuries.
items.random_wrong: Ireland and Britain were never linked.
items.why: Issues of land, religion and rule stretch back hundreds of years.

items.q: Did the partition of Ireland (1920–21) end the conflict?
items.correct: No — it created Northern Ireland but left divisions that later fuelled the Troubles.
items.why: Partition was a turning point, not a final resolution.
